text:
emily: FYI customer 'Acme Analytics' getting 403 when using SSO-created token. They call POST /v1/predict and get an 'invalid_scope' style message. Customer thinks it's an API key problem but they're on OAuth SSO flow.
kevin: Any chance they're hitting a plan/feature gate? last week we saw feature flags surface as scope errors for OAuth flows.
emily: Looks like that. Support logs show token scopes: [\"inference.basic\"] but the endpoint expects priority-inference for ephemeral priority tier traffic. Response body from our API:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "access_denied",
  "error_description": "invalid_scope: missing priority_inference"
}
```
ashley: Do we have billing sku for that tenant? if they paid for priority, entitlement should be set on account.
jordan: Billing shows SKU 'standard-infer' not 'priority-infer'. So entitlement not present. However customer says their sales order added priority yesterday.
emily: Repro steps I used:
1) Exchange SSO code -> token using our oauth endpoint
2) Call /v1/predict with Authorization: Bearer <token>
3) 403 as above
curl snippet:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/predict \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
kevin: This looks like the entitlement service hasn't picked up the billing change OR there's a mapping bug: entitlement -> oauth scope mapping defaults to returning only base scopes for SSO tokens until entitlement cache refresh. That yields 'invalid_scope' even though UI shows feature enabled.
emily: Found a cache mismatch in logs: entitlement-cache missed tenant update at 2025-11-02T09:12Z. Support-bot created ticket #SUP-12345.
support-bot: Ticket SUP-12345 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P2.
ashley: Short-term workaround: create a console API key (non-SSO) for customer; API keys bypass oauth scope mapping and check entitlement directly at API-key path (which currently reads billing synchronously). That gets them unblocked while we fix mapping.
jordan: I'll coordinate with billing to re-push the SKU sync and force entitlement refresh for tenant acme-123.
kevin: Engineering follow-up: eng-runtime to add a fast-path that, if billing change timestamp > token issue time, re-evaluates entitlements for that request (prevents stale-cache false negatives). Filed ENG-789 to track.
emily: For support notes: tenant acme-123, affected endpoints /v1/predict, token flow: OAuth SSO, workaround: create console API key or ask billing to re-sync. Mark as escalated to eng-runtime + billing. Customer notified with workaround.
ashley: :white_check_mark: I'll send the workaround steps and ask for screenshot of the token scopes.
kevin: Assign to me for a short hotfix. I'll also add an observability alert for entitlement-cache misses mapping to oauth scopes.
emily: Thanks — keeping this thread for updates.
